items.title: CISA Adds Three Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.description: CISA has added three new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-120705 OSGeo GeoServer XML Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-129243 OSGeo GeoServer Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability  CVE-2026-136716 Drupal Core Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions Vulnerability  These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

items.title: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software
items.description: View CSAF Summary Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow attackers to corrupt application memory and cause instability or a crash, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution, if a user is convinced to open a malicious file. The following versions of AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software are affected: C-More EA9 Programming Software <=V6.80 (CVE-2026-127280) CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 7.8 AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software 1 Vulnerability Heap-based Buffer Overflow Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Water and Wastewater Systems Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: United States Vulnerabilities CVE-2026-127280 C-More EA9 Programming Software V6.80 does not adequately validate data read from a project file before using it in heap memory operations. A crafted file causes a heap buffer overrun during file open, resulting in heap corruption and instability within the application. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by convincing a user to open a malicious project file delivered through common distribution channels such as email, file sharing, or removable media. Read More 1 Affected Product AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software <=V6.80 Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Update C-More EA9 Programming Software to V6.81: https://www.automationdirect.com/support/software-downloads Mitigation If you cannot update to the latest software or firmware version right away, apply the following compensating controls to reduce risk until the update can be performed. These measures are temporary and do not replace the update, which remains the primary and recommended remediation. Apply these controls as appropriate based on the vulnerability, assessed risk, operational requirements, and characteristics of your environment. Implement changes under your established management-of-change process. Before implementing isolation, access-control, or network-configuration changes, evaluate potential impacts to safety, availability, and essential operational functions. • Isolate affected engineering workstations and OT systems from external and nonessential networks, including the internet and corporate IT networks, where operationally feasible. • Disable or tightly restrict vendor, contractor, and other remote access to the affected OT environment until the vulnerability can be remediated. Where remote access is operationally required, use a hardened jump host, enforce multi-factor authentication, apply least-privilege access, and limit access to authorized, time-bound sessions. • Use trusted, dedicated OT networks for device communication. Where practicable and appropriate to the assessed risk, use dedicated or physically separated infrastructure for higher-criticality systems. Where logical segmentation is used, ensure segmentation controls are appropriately configured, secured, and monitored. • Restrict both physical and logical access to affected systems to authorized personnel only. Apply least-privilege principles to administrative, engineering, maintenance, and service access. • Configure application allowlisting, where supported, so that only trusted and pre-approved applications are permitted to execute. Block unauthorized software. • Use appropriate antivirus or endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools where supported and compatible with the affected system. Configure host-based and network firewalls to permit only required communications. • Disable unnecessary services, ports, protocols, and communication pathways associated with the affected systems. Where a service or protocol cannot be disabled for operational reasons, restrict access to trusted systems and authorized users wherever possible. • Enable and regularly review available system, security, and network logs to identify suspicious or unauthorized activity. Where appropriate, monitor communications to and from affected systems for unexpected connections or changes in network behavior. • Maintain secure, tested, and preferably offline backups of PLC programs, device configurations, engineering workstation configurations, and other information necessary to restore operations. Periodically verify that backups can be successfully restored. • Verify that critical OT functions can continue operating without unnecessary dependencies on external networks, cloud services, remote-access services, corporate IT services, or other nonessential systems. • If removable media is required to transfer files into an isolated or restricted environment, use controlled and trusted media and scan it for malicious content before use. • Continuously evaluate the risks associated with operating vulnerable or outdated firmware or software. Adjust compensating controls as the threat environment, operational requirements, or available vulnerability information changes. These compensating controls are intended to reduce exposure while remediation is pending. Organizations should prioritize applying the vendor-provided update as soon as it can be safely tested and deployed within the operational environment. Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-122 Heap-based Buffer Overflow CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 7.8 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H 4.0 8.4 HIGH CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N View CVE Details Acknowledgments rgod of TrendAI Zero Day Initiative reported this vulnerability to CISA.   Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet . Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics . Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies . CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets . Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies . Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. items.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.description: CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation.  CVE-2024-10441 Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output Vulnerability CVE-2026-40217 BerriAI LiteLLM Unprotected Alternate Channel Vulnerability CVE-2026-90436 Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability CVE-2026-90817 Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.  Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.  While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria .  Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

items.title: Critical Java Vulnerability Requires Immediate Patching
items.description: Purpose CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed Oracle Java vulnerability CVE-2026-114938 . This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as “Java4Shell,” affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which is part of the Java Development Kit (JDK). Specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow for unauthenticated remote code execution. Actions to take CISA urges organizations to take the following actions: Identify affected Java installations. Review your software inventory for JDKs and Java runtimes, including those bundled with third-party applications or included in container images and appliances. Note: JDKs and Java runtimes may not appear as separate entries in software inventories. Apply relevant Java and vendor patches as soon as they are available, prioritizing internet-facing systems. If immediate patching is not feasible, implement temporary compensating controls, such as restricting and validating Base64 input at the application boundary, enforcing input-size limits, and limiting unauthenticated access. Review Oracle’s security advisory for guidance on patching and affected products and versions.  Monitor for indicators of suspicious activity, including rogue runtimes, unexpected JVM crashes, and suspicious Java processes.
